scope: feature branch 031-base-image vs origin/main (git diff origin/main...HEAD), excluding specs/031-base-image records other than spec.md and decisions.md; read past the diff into fairdm/conf/setup.py, docs/portal-development/configuration.md, .dockerignore, tests.yml, tag-release.yml and publish.yml

findings.claim: Following the deployment guide bakes a portal's production secrets into its image. The example Dockerfile copies the whole portal root into the runtime image, the guide never mentions a .dockerignore, and FairDM's own configuration page tells portals to put DJANGO_SECRET_KEY and DATABASE_URL in stack.production.env in that root. The image sets DJANGO_ENV=production, so fairdm.setup() reads that file inside the container. The image works and nothing warns anyone that the secrets are in a layer.
findings.evidence: docker/portal.Dockerfile:13 `COPY --chown=fairdm:fairdm . .` (build stage) and :19 `COPY --chown=fairdm:fairdm . /app` (runtime stage, what ships). docs/portal-development/production.md:60-66 says 'Copy the Dockerfile below to your portal's repository' and the page has no .dockerignore and no warning about files in the build context. docs/portal-development/configuration.md:275-285 'Production Setup' shows `# stack.production.env` holding DJANGO_SECRET_KEY and DATABASE_URL with a password. fairdm/conf/setup.py:232-245 reads stack.env and stack.<DJANGO_ENV>.env from base_dir. docker/Dockerfile:38 sets DJANGO_ENV=production. FairDM's own .dockerignore excludes **/.env and **/.git but not stack*.env, and the guide does not tell a portal to write one at all, so .git, with any secret ever committed, goes into the image too.
findings.reproduction: A portal laid out as configuration.md describes has stack.production.env beside manage.py. The developer copies portal.Dockerfile and runs `docker build --build-arg FAIRDM_VERSION=0.2.0 -t my-portal .`, then `docker run --rm --entrypoint cat my-portal /app/stack.production.env`. That prints the secret key and the database password. Anyone who can pull the image, from a public ghcr package, a CI cache or a shared registry, gets them: the secret key forges sessions and password-reset tokens.
findings.suggested_fix: In production.md, next to the example Dockerfile, add a 'Keep secrets out of the image' paragraph with an example .dockerignore listing at least `stack*.env`, `.env`, `.git` and `.venv`, and say that production secrets come from the container's environment at run time, never from a file in the build context. Make configuration.md's 'Production Setup' say that stack.production.env is for a host deployment and must never be copied into an image. No code change is needed.

findings.claim: The Image job holds a GITHUB_TOKEN with packages: write on every run: same-repository pull requests, every push to main and manual runs. Only release-tag runs publish. On every other run the token can still overwrite any tag of ghcr.io/fair-dm/fairdm, and FR-013 ('a published tag MUST NOT be moved') then rests on no code in that run misbehaving. actions/checkout also leaves the token in .git/config by default, so every later step, including the branch's own docker/smoke-test.sh, can read it. Forks are not exposed, because GitHub gives pull_request runs from forks a read-only token and no secrets.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/image.yml:28-30 sets `permissions: contents: read, packages: write` on the single job, whose triggers at :7-14 are pull_request, push to main, release and workflow_dispatch. Publishing is gated only per step, at :121 and :129 (`if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')`). :57-58 calls `actions/checkout@v7` without `persist-credentials: false`. Third-party actions run in the same job: docker/setup-buildx-action@v4 (:71) and docker/build-push-action@v7 (:74, :88), plus docker/smoke-test.sh from the checked-out ref at :116.
findings.reproduction: On a push to main, any step in the job, such as a compromised docker/build-push-action@v7 release or a change to smoke-test.sh merged to main, can run `git config --get http.https://github.com/.extraheader` to get the token, then `docker login ghcr.io` and `docker push ghcr.io/fair-dm/fairdm:0.2.0`. Released tag 0.2.0 is replaced, and publish.sh's skip-existing check never runs.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the login and publish steps into a second job: `needs: Image`, `if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')`, with `packages: write` on that job only. Leave the build-and-smoke-test job at `contents: read`. Either rebuild from the warm cache in the publish job, or pass the images across as an artifact. Add `persist-credentials: false` to the checkout in both jobs. Afterwards, check that a pull_request run's token has no packages scope.

findings.claim: The guide tells portals that 'A published tag is never replaced', but the registry does not enforce that. publish.sh skips an existing tag, so it is a property of the script only. Anything else holding packages: write on the package can move a tag, and the guide offers portals no way to pin an image they cannot have swapped under them. The portal Dockerfile's `${FAIRDM_IMAGE}:${FAIRDM_VERSION}-dev` form also rules out a digest pin.
findings.evidence: docs/portal-development/production.md:31-33 'A published tag is never replaced.' docker/publish.sh:13-16 and :45-52 (the existence check, then `docker push`) is the only guard. docker/portal.Dockerfile:10 and :17 build the reference by string concatenation, so `FAIRDM_VERSION=0.2.0@sha256:…` produces `0.2.0@sha256:…-dev`, which is invalid.
findings.reproduction: Through SEC-002, or through any other workflow or person with write access to the ghcr package, push a different image as 0.2.0. A portal that rebuilds with FAIRDM_VERSION=0.2.0 silently picks it up.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword production.md:32-33 to 'FairDM's release workflow never replaces a published tag', and add one sentence: a portal that needs a fixed image pins the digest the release shows, in FROM lines written by hand. No change to the script.

findings.claim: The published images and the job that holds packages: write depend on references that can move. The docker/* actions are pinned to major-version tags, not commit SHAs. That follows the repository's existing convention, but these are new third-party actions, and docker/login-action is handed GITHUB_TOKEN directly. The base layers also come from floating tags, `python:3.13-slim` and `ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.11`, so a release image contains whatever those tags pointed at during the build, and nothing records which digest that was.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/image.yml:71 `docker/setup-buildx-action@v4`, :74 and :88 `docker/build-push-action@v7`, :122 `docker/login-action@v4` with `password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}` at :126. docker/Dockerfile:7 `FROM python:3.13-slim` and :28 `COPY --from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.11`.
findings.reproduction: If the v4 tag of docker/login-action is moved to a malicious commit, the next release run hands it a token that can push to ghcr.io/fair-dm/fairdm.
findings.suggested_fix: Pin docker/login-action and docker/build-push-action to full commit SHAs, keeping the version in a trailing comment. These are the two actions that touch the token or the pushed image. Dependabot's github-actions ecosystem keeps SHA pins current. Pinning the base images by digest can wait for a follow-up issue.

findings.claim: The guide's run example puts the secret key and the database password on the docker command line, where they are kept in shell history and are visible in the host's process list while the command runs.
findings.evidence: docs/portal-development/production.md:93-101: `--env DJANGO_SECRET_KEY=<at least 50 random characters>` and `--env POSTGRES_PASSWORD=<database password>`.
findings.reproduction: Run the example as written, then `history | grep SECRET_KEY` on the host prints the key.
findings.suggested_fix: Show `--env-file /path/outside/the/build/context/portal.env` for the secret values, or pass-through `--env DJANGO_SECRET_KEY` with the value already set in the operator's environment. Keep the variables table as it is.

findings.claim: The portal compose file in the guide publishes the development server on every interface of the developer's machine. The development image runs with DEBUG=True and ALLOWED_HOSTS=['*'], so anyone on the same network gets full tracebacks, with settings and local variables, from a developer's portal.
findings.evidence: docs/portal-development/production.md:234-236 `ports: - "8000:8000"` with `runserver 0.0.0.0:8000`. docker/Dockerfile:58 sets DJANGO_ENV=development. fairdm/conf/development.py:19 `DEBUG = True` and :31 `ALLOWED_HOSTS = ["*"]`.
findings.reproduction: Run `docker compose up` on a laptop on shared Wi-Fi. Another machine requests http://<laptop-ip>:8000/<a path that raises> and receives the Django debug page.
findings.suggested_fix: In the guide's compose example, publish as `"127.0.0.1:8000:8000"`. FairDM's own docker-compose.yml, which already did this before the branch, can take the same edit.

findings.claim: If the portal process is compromised, it can rewrite the portal's own code and, depending on how BuildKit copies ownership across stages, its installed packages. A foothold in one request then survives gunicorn worker restarts until the container is recreated. Decision D9 accepted this, and FR-004 does not forbid it. It is recorded here only so the trade is visible on the pull request.
findings.evidence: docker/portal.Dockerfile:19 `COPY --chown=fairdm:fairdm . /app` makes every source file owned by the server's user. docker/Dockerfile:26 `chown -R fairdm:fairdm /app /opt/venv`. portal.Dockerfile:18 copies /opt/venv from a stage where the fairdm user created it, with no --chown. Only /app/static and /app/media need to be writable (fairdm/conf/settings/static_media.py:18, :32). /docker-entrypoint.d, the entrypoint and uv stay root-owned, which is correct. specs/031-base-image/decisions.md D9 records the choice.
findings.reproduction: A code-execution bug in the portal writes to /app/config/wsgi.py or /opt/venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/…. The next gunicorn worker that starts imports the modified file.
findings.suggested_fix: None required for this pull request. If it is revisited, drop `--chown` from the runtime-stage COPY at portal.Dockerfile:19, add `--chown=root:root` to the /opt/venv COPY at :18, and leave /app, /app/static and /app/media owned by fairdm as docker/Dockerfile already creates them.

notes: Fork pull requests: the Image job requests packages: write, but for a pull_request from a fork GitHub forces a read-only GITHUB_TOKEN and passes no secrets, and the publish steps are gated on refs/tags/v. No path from a fork reaches a publish. This assumes FAIR-DM/fairdm is public and the private-repo option 'send write tokens to workflows from fork pull requests' is off. I could not check either offline.

Cache poisoning: the gha build caches and the uv actions/cache are scoped by ref. A pull request writes only its own scope, and release-tag runs restore from their own ref or the default branch, so a fork cannot poison a release build.

Script injection: image.yml takes the tag only through GITHUB_REF and GITHUB_REF_NAME environment variables (:64-67, :130), never `${{ github.* }}` inside `run:`, and publish.sh quotes every expansion. The tag reaches build-args as a single list item. No injection path found.

Tag overwrite through concurrency: release and workflow_dispatch runs on the same tag share the group `image-${{ github.ref }}` with cancel-in-progress false, so they are serialised and publish.sh's check-then-push cannot race itself.

test-suite.yml running as root in the container: the bind mount is the runner's own checkout and uv cache on an ephemeral hosted runner, CODECOV_TOKEN is not passed into the container, and tests.yml grants contents: read only. Root in the container gains nothing the runner user, who already has sudo, lacks. Pull request code also ran with the same token before this branch.

entrypoint.sh start steps: /docker-entrypoint.d is created root-owned with mode 755 (docker/Dockerfile:25, not in the chown), so the server user cannot plant a step. FAIRDM_START_DIR is operator-controlled environment.
publish.sh tests (tests/test_docker/test_publish.py, 11 tests swept): the skip-existing, error-before-push and partial-set cases assert the exact list of pushes, so none can pass vacuously.

Read past the diff: 6 files outside the diff opened for this lens (fairdm/conf/setup.py, docs/portal-development/configuration.md, .dockerignore, .github/workflows/tests.yml, tag-release.yml, publish.yml). The release is created with RELEASE_TOKEN, so the `release: published` trigger does fire.
